signals.name: Mobile Device Connection Not Controlled
signals.description: Mobile device connections to organizational systems are not restricted or monitored. This signal indicates that mobile devices may connect to systems without appropriate authorization, security verification, or connection controls.
signals.applicability: Applicable to all mobile device management configurations. Includes smartphones, tablets, and other mobile devices connecting to organizational systems, MDM solutions, and mobile access policies.

metadata.detection_notes: Detected through MDM configuration review, mobile device policy assessment, and connection monitoring analysis.

sources.title: 32 CFR Part 170 - Cybersecurity Maturity Model Certification Program

signals.name: Authorized Access Enforcement Not Implemented
signals.description: Systems do not enforce access decisions based on user authorization status. This signal indicates that access may be granted without verifying that users are authorized for the requested resources or operations.
signals.applicability: Applicable to all system access control implementations. Includes authentication systems, authorization mechanisms, and access decision points across applications and infrastructure.

metadata.detection_notes: Detected through access control mechanism review, authorization testing, and access decision audit.

sources.title: 32 CFR Part 170 - Cybersecurity Maturity Model Certification Program

signals.name: Concurrent Session Control Not Implemented
signals.description: The number of concurrent sessions for user accounts is not limited or monitored. This signal indicates that users may establish multiple simultaneous sessions, which may indicate credential sharing or compromise.
signals.applicability: Applicable to all systems with user authentication. Includes web applications, remote access services, and multi-session capable systems where concurrent session limits should be enforced.

metadata.detection_notes: Detected through session management configuration review, concurrent session monitoring, and authentication policy assessment.

sources.title: 32 CFR Part 170 - Cybersecurity Maturity Model Certification Program

signals.name: CUI Flow Not Controlled
signals.description: The flow of Controlled Unclassified Information (CUI) between systems, networks, or organizational boundaries is not controlled or restricted. This signal indicates that CUI may be transmitted or shared without appropriate authorization or technical controls.
signals.applicability: Applicable to systems processing, storing, or transmitting CUI. Includes data loss prevention controls, network segmentation, and information flow policies between security domains.

metadata.detection_notes: Detected through review of DLP configurations, network segmentation policies, and information flow controls between systems handling CUI.

sources.title: 32 CFR Part 170 - Cybersecurity Maturity Model Certification Program

signals.name: External System Connections Not Controlled
signals.description: Connections to external systems are not verified or controlled before allowing access to organizational systems. This signal indicates that external system connections may bypass security verification and authorization processes.
signals.applicability: Applicable to all external system interconnections. Includes connections to partner systems, cloud services, third-party APIs, and any external information systems accessing organizational resources.

metadata.detection_notes: Detected through external connection inventory review, interconnection agreement verification, and network boundary monitoring.

sources.title: 32 CFR Part 170 - Cybersecurity Maturity Model Certification Program

signals.name: Least Privilege Not Enforced
signals.description: Access permissions granted to users, accounts, or processes exceed what is necessary to perform assigned duties or functions. This signal indicates that the principle of least privilege is not applied, resulting in broader access rights than required for the intended purpose.
signals.applicability: Applicable to any system, application, or service where user or process permissions are configured. Includes IAM policies, role-based access control systems, file system permissions, database grants, and service account configurations.

metadata.detection_notes: Detected through analysis of IAM policies, role assignments, and permission configurations. May involve comparison of granted permissions against documented job functions or access requirements.

sources.title: 32 CFR Part 170 - Cybersecurity Maturity Model Certification Program

signals.name: Portable Storage Device Use Not Controlled
signals.canonical_name: Portable Storage Device Use Not Controlled
signals.description: The use of portable storage devices on organizational systems is not restricted or monitored. This signal indicates that removable media may be used without authorization, increasing risk of data exfiltration or malware introduction.
signals.applicability: Applicable to all systems where portable storage devices may be connected. Includes USB ports, card readers, and other interfaces for removable media on workstations, servers, and network devices.

metadata.detection_notes: Detected through endpoint device control policy review, USB port restrictions verification, and removable media usage monitoring.

sources.title: 32 CFR Part 170 - Cybersecurity Maturity Model Certification Program

signals.name: Privacy and Security Notice Missing
signals.description: Systems do not display approved privacy and security notices before granting access. This signal indicates that users may not be informed of usage terms, monitoring policies, or acceptable use requirements before accessing systems.
signals.applicability: Applicable to all systems requiring user login including workstations, servers, applications, and network devices. Includes login banners, terms of use acknowledgment, and consent notices.

metadata.detection_notes: Detected through review of login banner configurations, pre-authentication notices, and terms acceptance mechanisms.

sources.title: 32 CFR Part 170 - Cybersecurity Maturity Model Certification Program

signals.name: Privileged Function Execution Not Logged
signals.description: Execution of privileged functions is not logged or audited. This signal indicates that administrative actions and security-relevant operations may occur without accountability or traceability.
signals.applicability: Applicable to all systems where privileged functions are executed. Includes administrative consoles, security tools, system configuration interfaces, and any privileged access points.

metadata.detection_notes: Detected through audit log configuration review, privileged action monitoring assessment, and SIEM integration verification.

sources.title: 32 CFR Part 170 - Cybersecurity Maturity Model Certification Program

signals.name: Privileged Remote Access Not Separately Authenticated
signals.canonical_name: Privileged Remote Access Not Separately Authenticated
signals.description: Privileged commands executed via remote access are not authenticated separately from initial session authentication. This signal indicates that elevated privileges may be exercised without additional verification.
signals.applicability: Applicable to all privileged remote access scenarios. Includes remote administrative sessions, privileged access management systems, and any remote elevation of privileges.

metadata.detection_notes: Detected through remote access authentication flow review, privileged session management assessment, and step-up authentication verification.

sources.title: 32 CFR Part 170 - Cybersecurity Maturity Model Certification Program

signals.name: Remote Access Not Through Managed Access Points
signals.canonical_name: Remote Access Not Through Managed Access Points
signals.description: Remote access to organizational systems does not route through managed network access control points. This signal indicates that remote connections may bypass security monitoring, filtering, and access controls.
signals.applicability: Applicable to all remote access configurations. Includes VPN gateways, remote desktop services, jump servers, and any mechanisms for external access to organizational systems.

metadata.detection_notes: Detected through remote access architecture review, network access point inventory, and traffic flow analysis.

sources.title: 32 CFR Part 170 - Cybersecurity Maturity Model Certification Program

signals.name: Separation of Duties Not Enforced
signals.description: Critical functions are not divided among different individuals to reduce the risk of malicious activity without collusion. This signal indicates that single individuals may have the ability to perform security-critical actions without oversight or checks.
signals.applicability: Applicable to systems and processes where separation of duties is required to prevent fraud or error. Includes financial systems, privileged access management, change management, and security administration.

metadata.detection_notes: Detected through role assignment analysis, workflow review, and assessment of dual-control requirements for critical functions.

sources.title: 32 CFR Part 170 - Cybersecurity Maturity Model Certification Program

signals.name: Session Lock Not Configured
signals.description: System sessions are not configured to lock or terminate after a period of inactivity. This signal indicates that idle sessions remain active indefinitely without requiring re-authentication, potentially allowing unauthorized access to unattended systems.
signals.applicability: Applicable to workstations, servers, cloud consoles, applications, and any system where user sessions are established. Includes operating system screen lock policies, web application session timeouts, SSH session configurations, and remote desktop settings.

metadata.detection_notes: Detected through review of group policy settings, session timeout configurations, screen lock policies, and application session management parameters.

sources.title: 32 CFR Part 170 - Cybersecurity Maturity Model Certification Program

signals.name: Session Termination Not Implemented
signals.description: User sessions are not automatically terminated after a period of inactivity or when no longer needed. This signal indicates that stale sessions may remain active, creating opportunities for unauthorized access.
signals.applicability: Applicable to all systems with user sessions. Includes web applications, remote access sessions, administrative consoles, and any interactive system access.

metadata.detection_notes: Detected through session timeout configuration review, idle session testing, and session management policy assessment.

sources.title: 32 CFR Part 170 - Cybersecurity Maturity Model Certification Program

signals.name: Transaction and Function Access Not Controlled
signals.canonical_name: Transaction and Function Access Not Controlled
signals.description: Access to security-relevant transactions and system functions is not restricted based on user roles or authorization levels. This signal indicates that users may execute sensitive operations without appropriate access controls.
signals.applicability: Applicable to all systems with security-relevant functions. Includes administrative interfaces, configuration management systems, security tool access, and transaction processing systems.

metadata.detection_notes: Detected through role-based access control review, function-level authorization testing, and transaction access audit.

sources.title: 32 CFR Part 170 - Cybersecurity Maturity Model Certification Program

signals.name: Unsuccessful Logon Attempts Not Limited
signals.description: Systems do not limit or respond to unsuccessful logon attempts. This signal indicates that accounts may be vulnerable to brute force or password guessing attacks without lockout or delay mechanisms.
signals.applicability: Applicable to all authentication systems including operating systems, applications, network devices, and cloud services. Includes account lockout policies, rate limiting, and progressive delays.

metadata.detection_notes: Detected through review of account lockout policies, authentication rate limiting configurations, and failed login monitoring.

sources.title: 32 CFR Part 170 - Cybersecurity Maturity Model Certification Program

signals.name: CUI on Portable Storage Not Encrypted
signals.canonical_name: CUI on Portable Storage Not Encrypted
signals.description: Controlled Unclassified Information stored on portable storage devices is not encrypted. This signal indicates that CUI may be exposed if portable storage devices are lost, stolen, or improperly accessed.
signals.applicability: Applicable to all portable storage devices containing CUI. Includes USB drives, external hard drives, SD cards, and other removable media used to store or transport CUI.

metadata.detection_notes: Detected through portable storage encryption policy review, device encryption status verification, and DLP monitoring for unencrypted CUI transfers.

sources.title: 32 CFR Part 170 - Cybersecurity Maturity Model Certification Program

signals.name: Publicly Accessible System Content Not Controlled
signals.canonical_name: Publicly Accessible System Content Not Controlled
signals.description: Content posted on publicly accessible systems is not reviewed or controlled before publication. This signal indicates that sensitive or unauthorized information may be inadvertently disclosed through public-facing systems.
signals.applicability: Applicable to all publicly accessible organizational systems. Includes public websites, external APIs, file sharing services, and any systems accessible from the internet that publish organizational content.

metadata.detection_notes: Detected through content review process assessment, public system configuration review, and monitoring for inadvertent CUI disclosure.

sources.title: 32 CFR Part 170 - Cybersecurity Maturity Model Certification Program

signals.name: Remote Access Without Monitoring or Control
signals.canonical_name: Remote Access Without Monitoring or Control
signals.description: Remote access to systems is permitted without mechanisms for monitoring, controlling, or restricting such connections. This signal indicates that remote access pathways exist without visibility into connection activity or the ability to enforce access policies.
signals.applicability: Applicable to any system allowing remote connections including VPN gateways, remote desktop services, SSH access, cloud management interfaces, and remote administration tools. Includes both user and automated remote access scenarios.

metadata.detection_notes: Detected through review of network architecture, firewall rules, VPN configurations, and remote access service settings. May involve analysis of logging configurations and access control mechanisms for remote pathways.

sources.title: 32 CFR Part 170 - Cybersecurity Maturity Model Certification Program

signals.name: Unrestricted Administrative Access
signals.description: Administrative or privileged access to a system, service, or resource is not restricted by defined conditions or constraints. This signal indicates that administrative privileges are available without limitations such as network boundaries, time-based restrictions, multi-factor authentication requirements, or role-based scoping.
signals.applicability: Applicable to any system, cloud service, infrastructure component, or application where administrative access is configured. Includes identity providers, cloud management consoles, server administration interfaces, database management systems, and network device configurations.

metadata.detection_notes: Commonly detected through analysis of IAM policies, role configurations, conditional access policies, and network access control lists. May also be identified through review of authentication configuration and session management settings.

sources.title: 32 CFR Part 170 - Cybersecurity Maturity Model Certification Program

signals.name: Wireless Authentication Not Implemented
signals.description: Wireless networks do not require authentication using strong cryptographic mechanisms. This signal indicates that wireless access may be granted without verifying user or device identity through secure authentication protocols.
signals.applicability: Applicable to all wireless network authentication configurations. Includes 802.1X/EAP authentication, WPA2/WPA3-Enterprise, certificate-based authentication, and RADIUS integration.

metadata.detection_notes: Detected through wireless security configuration review, authentication protocol analysis, and RADIUS/authentication server settings.

sources.title: 32 CFR Part 170 - Cybersecurity Maturity Model Certification Program

signals.name: Wireless Access Not Controlled
signals.description: Wireless network access is not managed, monitored, or restricted according to security policies. This signal indicates that wireless connections may be established without appropriate authorization or security controls.
signals.applicability: Applicable to all wireless network infrastructure including Wi-Fi access points, wireless controllers, and client device policies. Includes wireless access control, network segmentation, and rogue AP detection.

metadata.detection_notes: Detected through wireless network configuration review, access point security settings, and wireless policy assessment.

sources.title: 32 CFR Part 170 - Cybersecurity Maturity Model Certification Program

signals.name: Continuous Security Monitoring Not Implemented
signals.description: Continuous monitoring of security controls and system security status is not implemented. This signal indicates that security changes and threats may not be detected in real-time.
signals.applicability: Applicable to all organizational security monitoring. Includes automated security monitoring, real-time alerting, and ongoing security status reporting.

metadata.detection_notes: Detected through monitoring capability review, real-time alerting assessment, and security dashboard verification.

sources.title: 32 CFR Part 170 - Cybersecurity Maturity Model Certification Program

signals.name: Periodic Security Review Not Conducted
signals.description: Security controls are not periodically reviewed to ensure ongoing effectiveness. This signal indicates that control degradation or security drift may go undetected.
signals.applicability: Applicable to all security control implementations. Includes scheduled reviews, control testing, and effectiveness verification on a regular basis.

metadata.detection_notes: Detected through assessment schedule review, last assessment date verification, and control testing records analysis.

sources.title: 32 CFR Part 170 - Cybersecurity Maturity Model Certification Program

signals.name: Security Assessment Plan Not Defined
signals.description: A security assessment plan to periodically evaluate security controls is not developed or documented. This signal indicates that security control effectiveness may not be systematically verified.
signals.applicability: Applicable to all organizational security assessment activities. Includes assessment methodology, scope, frequency, and documentation requirements.

metadata.detection_notes: Detected through security assessment documentation review, methodology verification, and assessment schedule assessment.

sources.title: 32 CFR Part 170 - Cybersecurity Maturity Model Certification Program

signals.name: Plan of Action Not Maintained
signals.description: A Plan of Action and Milestones (POA&M) for addressing security deficiencies is not developed or maintained. This signal indicates that identified security gaps may not be tracked to resolution.
signals.applicability: Applicable to all identified security deficiencies. Includes vulnerability findings, assessment gaps, audit findings, and other security weaknesses requiring remediation.

metadata.detection_notes: Detected through POA&M documentation review, remediation tracking verification, and milestone progress assessment.

sources.title: 32 CFR Part 170 - Cybersecurity Maturity Model Certification Program

signals.name: Audit Storage Capacity Insufficient
signals.description: Insufficient storage capacity is allocated for audit log retention, risking loss of audit data. This signal indicates that audit records may be overwritten or deleted before required retention periods are met.
signals.applicability: Applicable to all systems generating audit logs. Includes log storage sizing, retention policies, and capacity monitoring for audit data.

metadata.detection_notes: Detected through log storage capacity assessment, retention policy review, and historical log availability verification.

signals.name: Audit Record Content Insufficient
signals.description: Audit records do not contain sufficient information to establish what events occurred, when they occurred, where they occurred, and who was involved. This signal indicates that audit logs may lack critical details needed for incident investigation.
signals.applicability: Applicable to all audit logging configurations. Includes event timestamp, source, user identity, event type, outcome, and affected resources in audit record format.

metadata.detection_notes: Detected through audit log format review, sample log analysis, and comparison against required audit content standards.

sources.title: NIST SP 800-171 Rev 2 - Audit and Accountability

signals.name: Centralized Audit Log Management Not Implemented
signals.canonical_name: Centralized Audit Log Management Not Implemented
signals.description: Audit logs are not centrally collected, managed, or analyzed. This signal indicates that log data may be fragmented across systems, making correlation and incident detection difficult.
signals.applicability: Applicable to all organizations with multiple systems generating audit logs. Includes SIEM solutions, log aggregation platforms, and centralized log management systems.

metadata.detection_notes: Detected through log management architecture review, SIEM deployment assessment, and log forwarding configuration verification.

sources.title: NIST SP 800-171 Rev 2 - Audit and Accountability
32 CFR Part 170 - Cybersecurity Maturity Model Certification Program

signals.name: Audit Record Correlation Not Implemented
signals.description: Audit records from different sources are not correlated to identify patterns indicating potential security incidents. This signal indicates that coordinated attacks or complex incidents may go undetected.
signals.applicability: Applicable to organizations with multiple log sources. Includes SIEM correlation rules, cross-system event analysis, and automated threat detection based on log patterns.

metadata.detection_notes: Detected through SIEM correlation rule review, automated alerting assessment, and cross-system analysis capability verification.

sources.title: NIST SP 800-171 Rev 2 - Audit and Accountability
32 CFR Part 170 - Cybersecurity Maturity Model Certification Program

signals.name: Audit Logging Not Enabled
signals.description: Systems, applications, or infrastructure components are not configured to generate audit logs for security-relevant events. This signal indicates that activities such as authentication attempts, access to sensitive resources, configuration changes, or administrative actions are not being recorded.
signals.applicability: Applicable to any system capable of generating audit logs including operating systems, applications, databases, network devices, cloud services, and security tools. Includes authentication events, authorization decisions, data access, and administrative operations.

metadata.detection_notes: Detected through review of logging configurations, audit policy settings, SIEM integrations, and log collection infrastructure. May involve checking for disabled audit policies or missing log forwarding configurations.

sources.title: NIST SP 800-171 Rev 2 - Audit and Accountability
32 CFR Part 170 - Cybersecurity Maturity Model Certification Program

signals.name: Non-Repudiation Controls Not Implemented
signals.description: Audit mechanisms do not provide non-repudiation capabilities to prove that actions occurred. This signal indicates that users may be able to deny performing actions due to lack of cryptographic or tamper-evident logging.
signals.applicability: Applicable to systems requiring strong accountability. Includes digitally signed logs, tamper-evident logging, write-once storage, and cryptographic timestamps.

metadata.detection_notes: Detected through audit integrity mechanism review, log signing verification, and tamper detection capability assessment.

sources.title: NIST SP 800-171 Rev 2 - Audit and Accountability
32 CFR Part 170 - Cybersecurity Maturity Model Certification Program

signals.name: Audit Logs Not Protected
signals.description: Audit logs are stored without adequate protection against unauthorized access, modification, or deletion. This signal indicates that the integrity and confidentiality of audit records may be compromised, reducing their value for security monitoring and forensic purposes.
signals.applicability: Applicable to any audit log storage location including local file systems, centralized log servers, cloud storage, and SIEM platforms. Includes access controls, encryption, and integrity verification mechanisms for log data.

metadata.detection_notes: Detected through review of log file permissions, access controls on logging infrastructure, encryption settings for log data at rest and in transit, and integrity verification mechanisms.

sources.title: NIST SP 800-171 Rev 2 - Audit and Accountability
32 CFR Part 170 - Cybersecurity Maturity Model Certification Program

signals.name: Audit Log Retention Not Configured
signals.description: Audit logs are not retained for an adequate period or are subject to automatic deletion without regard to retention requirements. This signal indicates that historical audit data may not be available for incident investigation, compliance verification, or forensic analysis.
signals.applicability: Applicable to any logging infrastructure including local log storage, centralized logging systems, SIEM platforms, and cloud-native logging services. Includes retention policies for security logs, application logs, and system logs.

metadata.detection_notes: Detected through review of log rotation configurations, retention policies, storage capacity planning, and archive procedures. May involve checking logrotate settings, cloud logging retention, or SIEM data lifecycle policies.

sources.title: NIST SP 800-171 Rev 2 - Audit and Accountability
32 CFR Part 170 - Cybersecurity Maturity Model Certification Program

signals.name: Audit Log Review Not Configured
signals.description: No automated or manual process exists to review audit logs for security-relevant events or anomalies. This signal indicates that collected audit data is not being analyzed, reducing the ability to detect unauthorized activities or security incidents.
signals.applicability: Applicable to any environment generating security audit logs. Includes SIEM alerting rules, log analysis processes, security monitoring configurations, and automated detection mechanisms.

metadata.detection_notes: Detected through review of SIEM configurations, alerting rules, log analysis procedures, and documentation of review processes. May involve checking for active detection rules or scheduled review tasks.

sources.title: NIST SP 800-171 Rev 2 - Audit and Accountability
32 CFR Part 170 - Cybersecurity Maturity Model Certification Program

signals.name: Insider Threat Awareness Training Not Provided
signals.canonical_name: Insider Threat Awareness Training Not Provided
signals.description: Personnel do not receive training on recognizing and reporting potential insider threat indicators. This signal indicates that employees may not understand how to identify suspicious behavior from colleagues or themselves.
signals.applicability: Applicable to all organizations handling CUI. Includes insider threat awareness programs, behavioral indicator training, and reporting procedure education.

metadata.detection_notes: Detected through insider threat training program review, training content assessment, and completion records verification.

sources.title: NIST SP 800-171 Rev 2 - Awareness and Training
32 CFR Part 170 - Cybersecurity Maturity Model Certification Program

signals.name: Role-Based Security Training Not Provided
signals.description: Personnel with security responsibilities do not receive specialized training appropriate to their roles. This signal indicates that administrators, developers, or security personnel may lack skills needed for their specific security duties.
signals.applicability: Applicable to personnel with specialized security responsibilities. Includes system administrators, security officers, developers, incident responders, and other roles requiring specific security competencies.

metadata.detection_notes: Detected through role-based training program review, specialized training records, and competency assessment verification.

sources.title: NIST SP 800-171 Rev 2 - Awareness and Training
32 CFR Part 170 - Cybersecurity Maturity Model Certification Program

signals.name: Security Awareness Training Not Provided
signals.description: Users do not receive security awareness training on recognizing and reporting potential security threats. This signal indicates that personnel may lack the knowledge to identify phishing, social engineering, or other security risks.
signals.applicability: Applicable to all organizations with personnel who access information systems. Includes security awareness programs, phishing training, and general security education for all users.

metadata.detection_notes: Detected through training program review, training completion records, and security awareness assessment.

sources.title: NIST SP 800-171 Rev 2 - Awareness and Training
32 CFR Part 170 - Cybersecurity Maturity Model Certification Program

signals.name: System Architecture Protection Not Implemented
signals.description: Security architecture principles such as defense in depth and least privilege are not implemented in system design. This signal indicates that the system may lack layered security controls.
signals.applicability: Applicable to all system architectures. Includes defense in depth, network segmentation, security zones, and architectural security controls.

metadata.detection_notes: Detected through architecture review, security zone assessment, and defense-in-depth verification.

sources.title: NIST SP 800-171 Rev 2 - System and Communications Protection
32 CFR Part 170 - Cybersecurity Maturity Model Certification Program

signals.name: Network Boundary Protection Not Implemented
signals.description: Communications at system and network boundaries are not monitored or controlled. This signal indicates that traffic entering or leaving security domains is not subject to inspection, filtering, or access controls.
signals.applicability: Applicable to network perimeters, cloud VPC boundaries, security zones, and any demarcation point between trust levels. Includes firewalls, network ACLs, security groups, and web application firewalls.

metadata.detection_notes: Detected through network architecture review, firewall and security group analysis, traffic flow inspection, and network segmentation assessment.

sources.title: NIST SP 800-171 Rev 2 - System and Communications Protection
32 CFR Part 170 - Cybersecurity Maturity Model Certification Program

signals.name: Collaborative Computing Device Control Not Implemented
signals.canonical_name: Collaborative Computing Device Control Not Implemented
signals.description: Collaborative computing devices such as cameras, microphones, and screen sharing are not controlled against unauthorized activation. This signal indicates that eavesdropping or surveillance may be possible.
signals.applicability: Applicable to all collaborative computing features. Includes webcams, microphones, screen sharing, remote desktop, and unified communications devices.

metadata.detection_notes: Detected through device policy review, camera/microphone control verification, and collaboration tool security assessment.

sources.title: NIST SP 800-171 Rev 2 - System and Communications Protection
32 CFR Part 170 - Cybersecurity Maturity Model Certification Program

signals.name: Covert Channel Detection Not Implemented
signals.description: Mechanisms to detect covert communication channels are not implemented. This signal indicates that data may be exfiltrated through hidden or non-standard communication methods.
signals.applicability: Applicable to systems requiring advanced threat protection. Includes DNS tunneling detection, steganography detection, and non-standard protocol monitoring.

metadata.detection_notes: Detected through covert channel analysis capability review, protocol anomaly detection, and non-standard traffic monitoring.

sources.title: NIST SP 800-171 Rev 2 - System and Communications Protection
32 CFR Part 170 - Cybersecurity Maturity Model Certification Program

signals.name: CUI at Rest Not Protected
signals.description: Controlled Unclassified Information stored in persistent storage is not protected through encryption or other mechanisms. This signal indicates that stored CUI may be exposed if physical or logical access is compromised.
signals.applicability: Applicable to all persistent CUI storage. Includes disk encryption, database encryption, file-level encryption, and storage access controls.

metadata.detection_notes: Detected through storage encryption configuration review, at-rest encryption verification, and CUI storage assessment.

sources.title: NIST SP 800-171 Rev 2 - System and Communications Protection
32 CFR Part 170 - Cybersecurity Maturity Model Certification Program

signals.name: DNS Protection Not Implemented
signals.description: DNS resolution is not protected against spoofing or manipulation attacks. This signal indicates that DNS responses may be forged to redirect traffic to malicious destinations.
signals.applicability: Applicable to all DNS resolution. Includes DNSSEC validation, DNS over HTTPS/TLS, internal DNS security, and DNS query monitoring.

metadata.detection_notes: Detected through DNS configuration review, DNSSEC verification, and DNS query protection assessment.

sources.title: NIST SP 800-171 Rev 2 - System and Communications Protection
32 CFR Part 170 - Cybersecurity Maturity Model Certification Program

signals.name: Data Not Encrypted at Rest
signals.description: Sensitive data stored in databases, file systems, backups, or other storage media is not encrypted. This signal indicates that data may be exposed if storage media is accessed by unauthorized parties or improperly disposed of.
signals.applicability: Applicable to any data storage including databases, file systems, object storage, backup media, removable storage, and mobile devices. Includes both structured and unstructured data storage.

metadata.detection_notes: Detected through review of storage encryption configurations, database encryption settings, disk encryption status, and cloud storage encryption policies.

sources.title: NIST SP 800-171 Rev 2 - System and Communications Protection
32 CFR Part 170 - Cybersecurity Maturity Model Certification Program

signals.name: Data Not Encrypted in Transit
signals.description: Data transmitted between systems, services, or networks is not encrypted. This signal indicates that sensitive information may be exposed to interception or eavesdropping during transmission over network connections.
signals.applicability: Applicable to any network communication including API calls, database connections, file transfers, email, and internal service communication. Includes both external-facing and internal network traffic.

metadata.detection_notes: Detected through network traffic analysis, protocol inspection, TLS configuration review, and service endpoint configuration analysis. May involve checking for HTTP vs HTTPS, unencrypted database connections, or plaintext protocols.

sources.title: NIST SP 800-171 Rev 2 - System and Communications Protection
32 CFR Part 170 - Cybersecurity Maturity Model Certification Program

signals.name: FIPS-Validated Cryptography Not Used
signals.description: Cryptographic modules are not FIPS 140-2/140-3 validated when protecting CUI. This signal indicates that cryptographic implementations may not meet federal security standards.
signals.applicability: Applicable to all cryptographic protection of CUI. Includes encryption modules, key management systems, and cryptographic libraries used for CUI protection.

metadata.detection_notes: Detected through cryptographic module validation verification, FIPS mode configuration review, and encryption library assessment.

sources.title: NIST SP 800-171 Rev 2 - System and Communications Protection
32 CFR Part 170 - Cybersecurity Maturity Model Certification Program

signals.name: Cryptographic Key Management Not Implemented
signals.description: Cryptographic keys are not managed throughout their lifecycle including generation, distribution, storage, and revocation. This signal indicates that weak key management may compromise cryptographic protections.
signals.applicability: Applicable to all cryptographic key usage. Includes key generation, key storage, key distribution, key rotation, and key revocation procedures.

metadata.detection_notes: Detected through key management procedure review, key storage security assessment, and key lifecycle verification.

sources.title: NIST SP 800-171 Rev 2 - System and Communications Protection
32 CFR Part 170 - Cybersecurity Maturity Model Certification Program

signals.name: Mobile Code Execution Not Controlled
signals.description: Mobile code such as JavaScript, ActiveX, and macros is not controlled or restricted. This signal indicates that malicious mobile code may execute without user awareness or authorization.
signals.applicability: Applicable to all systems executing mobile code. Includes browser security settings, macro restrictions, plugin controls, and script execution policies.

metadata.detection_notes: Detected through browser security policy review, macro restriction verification, and mobile code execution testing.

sources.title: NIST SP 800-171 Rev 2 - System and Communications Protection
32 CFR Part 170 - Cybersecurity Maturity Model Certification Program

signals.name: Network Connection Termination Not Controlled
signals.description: Network connections are not terminated at the end of sessions or after periods of inactivity. This signal indicates that stale network connections may remain available for exploitation.
signals.applicability: Applicable to all network sessions. Includes session timeout settings, connection lifecycle management, and inactive connection termination policies.

metadata.detection_notes: Detected through network session configuration review, timeout policy verification, and connection lifecycle testing.

sources.title: NIST SP 800-171 Rev 2 - System and Communications Protection
32 CFR Part 170 - Cybersecurity Maturity Model Certification Program

signals.name: Communication Session Authenticity Not Ensured
signals.description: Authenticity of communication sessions is not verified through cryptographic mechanisms. This signal indicates that session hijacking or man-in-the-middle attacks may be possible.
signals.applicability: Applicable to all authenticated communication sessions. Includes TLS certificate validation, session token protection, and mutual authentication requirements.

metadata.detection_notes: Detected through session authentication configuration review, certificate validation testing, and mutual authentication verification.

sources.title: NIST SP 800-171 Rev 2 - System and Communications Protection
32 CFR Part 170 - Cybersecurity Maturity Model Certification Program

signals.name: Shared System Resource Protection Not Implemented

signals.applicability: Applicable to any application accepting external input including web applications, APIs, command-line tools, and data processing systems. Includes form inputs, API parameters, file uploads, and data imports.

metadata.detection_notes: Detected through code review, static application security testing (SAST), dynamic application security testing (DAST), and penetration testing.

signals.name: Input Validation Not Implemented
signals.description: Applications do not validate input data before processing, creating vulnerability to injection attacks. This signal indicates that SQL injection, XSS, and command injection vulnerabilities may exist.
signals.applicability: Applicable to all applications accepting user input. Includes web applications, APIs, command-line tools, and any software processing external data.

metadata.detection_notes: Detected through application security testing, code review, and input validation assessment.

signals.name: Malware Protection Not Implemented
signals.description: Systems do not have malware detection and prevention mechanisms deployed. This signal indicates that endpoints, servers, or other systems lack antivirus, anti-malware, or endpoint detection and response capabilities.
signals.applicability: Applicable to all endpoints, servers, and systems capable of executing code. Includes workstations, servers, virtual machines, containers, and mobile devices.

metadata.detection_notes: Detected through endpoint inventory review, security agent deployment status, and EDR/AV console coverage reports.

signals.name: Security Monitoring Not Implemented
signals.description: Systems are not configured to detect or alert on security-relevant events such as attacks, unauthorized access attempts, or anomalous behavior. This signal indicates that security incidents may occur without detection.
signals.applicability: Applicable to all systems and networks requiring security monitoring. Includes intrusion detection systems, security information and event management, endpoint detection and response, and network traffic analysis.

metadata.detection_notes: Detected through review of monitoring tool deployment, SIEM coverage, IDS/IPS configurations, and alerting rule effectiveness.

signals.name: Security Patching Not Current
signals.description: Systems have not been updated with current security patches or are running software versions with known vulnerabilities. This signal indicates that systems may be exposed to exploits for publicly disclosed vulnerabilities.
signals.applicability: Applicable to all software components including operating systems, applications, libraries, firmware, and container images. Includes both first-party and third-party software.

metadata.detection_notes: Detected through vulnerability scanning, patch compliance reporting, software version analysis, and dependency auditing tools.

signals.name: Spam Protection Not Implemented
signals.description: Email systems do not implement spam filtering and protection mechanisms. This signal indicates that phishing, malware, and unwanted messages may reach users without filtering.
signals.applicability: Applicable to all email systems. Includes spam filtering, email security gateways, phishing detection, and malicious attachment scanning.

metadata.detection_notes: Detected through email security configuration review, spam filter deployment verification, and email gateway assessment.

signals.name: Maintenance Media Not Sanitized
signals.description: Media containing diagnostic or maintenance data is not sanitized before reuse or disposal. This signal indicates that sensitive information captured during maintenance may be exposed.
signals.applicability: Applicable to all media used during maintenance activities. Includes diagnostic logs, memory dumps, backup media, and any storage used to capture maintenance data.

metadata.detection_notes: Detected through maintenance media handling procedure review, sanitization record verification, and media tracking assessment.

signals.name: System Maintenance Not Controlled
signals.description: System maintenance activities are not performed according to documented procedures or schedules. This signal indicates that maintenance may be ad-hoc, undocumented, or performed without proper authorization.
signals.applicability: Applicable to all organizational systems requiring maintenance. Includes scheduled maintenance, emergency repairs, and routine servicing of hardware and software components.

metadata.detection_notes: Detected through maintenance procedure review, maintenance log analysis, and scheduled maintenance verification.

signals.name: Maintenance Personnel Not Supervised
signals.description: Personnel performing maintenance without required access authorizations are not supervised during maintenance activities. This signal indicates that unauthorized individuals may have unsupervised access to systems.
signals.applicability: Applicable to all maintenance scenarios involving personnel without proper clearances. Includes vendor technicians, contractors, and any maintenance personnel requiring escort or supervision.

metadata.detection_notes: Detected through maintenance supervision policy review, escort log verification, and personnel authorization assessment.

signals.name: Remote Maintenance Not Authorized
signals.description: Remote maintenance connections are established without proper authorization or authentication. This signal indicates that unauthorized parties may perform remote maintenance activities.
signals.applicability: Applicable to all remote maintenance access. Includes authorization workflows, MFA requirements, and access control for remote maintenance sessions.

metadata.detection_notes: Detected through remote access authorization review, MFA verification for maintenance, and access control assessment.

sources.title: 32 CFR Part 170 - Cybersecurity Maturity Model Certification Program

signals.name: Remote Maintenance Not Monitored
signals.description: Remote maintenance sessions are not monitored or recorded. This signal indicates that remote maintenance activities may occur without oversight, increasing risk of unauthorized changes.
signals.applicability: Applicable to all remote maintenance access. Includes remote support sessions, vendor remote access, and any off-site maintenance activities performed over network connections.

metadata.detection_notes: Detected through remote maintenance configuration review, session recording verification, and monitoring capability assessment.

signals.name: Maintenance Tools Not Controlled
signals.description: Tools used for system maintenance are not approved, controlled, or monitored. This signal indicates that unauthorized or compromised tools may be used during maintenance activities.
signals.applicability: Applicable to all maintenance tools and utilities. Includes diagnostic software, repair tools, remote support utilities, and any software or hardware used for maintenance purposes.

metadata.detection_notes: Detected through maintenance tool inventory review, tool authorization verification, and tool integrity checking.

signals.name: Media Access Not Controlled
signals.description: Access to media containing CUI is not restricted to authorized individuals. This signal indicates that sensitive media may be accessible to unauthorized personnel.
signals.applicability: Applicable to all media containing CUI. Includes physical access controls for storage locations, logical access controls for digital media, and access logging for sensitive media.

metadata.detection_notes: Detected through media access control review, storage location security assessment, and access log analysis.

signals.name: Media Accountability Not Maintained
signals.description: An inventory and tracking system for CUI-containing media is not maintained. This signal indicates that media may be lost or misplaced without detection.
signals.applicability: Applicable to all CUI-containing media. Includes media inventories, chain of custody records, check-in/check-out procedures, and asset tracking systems.

metadata.detection_notes: Detected through media inventory review, chain of custody verification, and asset tracking system assessment.

sources.title: 32 CFR Part 170 - Cybersecurity Maturity Model Certification Program

signals.name: CUI Media Not Marked
signals.description: Media containing Controlled Unclassified Information is not properly marked or labeled. This signal indicates that CUI media may not be identifiable, leading to improper handling or protection.
signals.applicability: Applicable to all media containing CUI. Includes physical labels, file headers, container markings, and any identification mechanisms for CUI-containing media.

metadata.detection_notes: Detected through media labeling review, marking standard compliance assessment, and CUI identification verification.

sources.title: 32 CFR Part 170 - Cybersecurity Maturity Model Certification Program

signals.name: Media Disposal Not Tracked
signals.description: Disposal or destruction of CUI-containing media is not documented or verified. This signal indicates that media may be improperly disposed of without confirmation of secure destruction.
signals.applicability: Applicable to all CUI media disposal processes. Includes destruction certificates, disposal logs, vendor verification, and media lifecycle completion records.

metadata.detection_notes: Detected through disposal record review, destruction certificate verification, and vendor compliance assessment.

sources.title: 32 CFR Part 170 - Cybersecurity Maturity Model Certification Program

signals.name: Media Physical Protection Insufficient
signals.description: Physical protection measures for CUI-containing media are inadequate against environmental threats or tampering. This signal indicates media may be vulnerable to damage, theft, or unauthorized modification.
signals.applicability: Applicable to physical protection of all CUI media. Includes fire protection, environmental controls, tamper-evident measures, and physical security mechanisms.

metadata.detection_notes: Detected through physical protection assessment, environmental control verification, and tamper evidence review.

sources.title: 32 CFR Part 170 - Cybersecurity Maturity Model Certification Program

signals.name: Media Protection Not Implemented
signals.description: Physical and digital storage media containing sensitive information is not protected from unauthorized access. This signal indicates that media may be accessed, copied, or removed without appropriate controls.
signals.applicability: Applicable to all storage media including removable devices, backup media, printed materials, and portable storage. Includes physical access controls, encryption, and media handling procedures.

metadata.detection_notes: Detected through review of media handling procedures, physical access controls for media storage, and encryption requirements for removable media.

sources.title: 32 CFR Part 170 - Cybersecurity Maturity Model Certification Program

signals.name: Media Sanitization Not Performed
signals.description: Storage media is disposed of or repurposed without proper sanitization to remove sensitive data. This signal indicates that data may remain recoverable from media after its intended lifecycle.
signals.applicability: Applicable to all storage media including hard drives, SSDs, USB devices, backup tapes, optical media, and cloud storage. Includes both physical destruction and logical sanitization methods.

metadata.detection_notes: Detected through review of media sanitization procedures, disposal records, and verification of sanitization methods used.

sources.title: 32 CFR Part 170 - Cybersecurity Maturity Model Certification Program

signals.name: Media Storage Not Controlled
signals.description: Physical storage locations for CUI-containing media are not secured or access-controlled. This signal indicates that media storage areas may allow unauthorized physical access.
signals.applicability: Applicable to all physical media storage locations. Includes server rooms, tape libraries, document storage, archive facilities, and any location where CUI media is stored.

metadata.detection_notes: Detected through storage facility security assessment, access control verification, and physical security audit.

sources.title: 32 CFR Part 170 - Cybersecurity Maturity Model Certification Program

signals.name: Media Transport Not Controlled
signals.description: Transportation of media containing CUI is not protected through approved custodians, secure packaging, or tracking mechanisms. This signal indicates media may be lost, stolen, or compromised during transport.
signals.applicability: Applicable to all media transport scenarios. Includes courier services, internal transport, shipping of backup media, and any movement of CUI-containing media between locations.

metadata.detection_notes: Detected through media transport procedure review, chain of custody verification, and transport tracking assessment.

sources.title: 32 CFR Part 170 - Cybersecurity Maturity Model Certification Program

signals.name: Personnel Screening Not Performed
signals.description: Background screening is not performed on individuals prior to granting access to CUI systems. This signal indicates that personnel with unknown or risky backgrounds may have access to sensitive information.
signals.applicability: Applicable to all personnel with access to CUI. Includes pre-employment background checks, periodic re-screening, and screening for contractors and third-party personnel.

metadata.detection_notes: Detected through HR process review, screening record verification, and personnel file audit.

sources.title: 32 CFR Part 170 - Cybersecurity Maturity Model Certification Program

signals.name: Personnel Termination Process Not Implemented
signals.description: Procedures for revoking access upon personnel termination are not defined or followed. This signal indicates that former employees or contractors may retain access to systems after separation.
signals.applicability: Applicable to all personnel access management. Includes termination checklists, access revocation procedures, and property retrieval processes for departing personnel.

metadata.detection_notes: Detected through termination process review, orphaned account discovery, and access revocation timeliness verification.

sources.title: 32 CFR Part 170 - Cybersecurity Maturity Model Certification Program

signals.name: Physical Access Control Not Implemented
signals.description: Physical access to facilities housing CUI systems is not controlled or restricted. This signal indicates that unauthorized individuals may gain physical access to sensitive areas.
signals.applicability: Applicable to all facilities containing CUI systems. Includes entry points, secure areas, data centers, and any physical locations requiring access control.

metadata.detection_notes: Detected through physical access control assessment, entry point review, and access mechanism testing.

sources.title: 32 CFR Part 170 - Cybersecurity Maturity Model Certification Program

signals.name: Physical Access Logs Not Maintained
signals.description: Audit logs of physical access to facilities are not maintained or reviewed. This signal indicates that physical access events cannot be investigated or monitored.
signals.applicability: Applicable to all physical access control systems. Includes badge reader logs, entry/exit records, and physical access audit trails.

metadata.detection_notes: Detected through access log configuration review, log retention assessment, and audit trail verification.

signals.name: Alternate Work Site Security Not Addressed
signals.canonical_name: Alternate Work Site Security Not Addressed
signals.description: Security controls for alternate work sites such as home offices are not implemented or verified. This signal indicates that CUI may be processed in environments without adequate physical protection.
signals.applicability: Applicable to all remote and alternate work locations. Includes home office security, remote work environments, and temporary work locations accessing CUI.

metadata.detection_notes: Detected through remote work policy review, alternate site security verification, and telework agreement assessment.

sources.title: 32 CFR Part 170 - Cybersecurity Maturity Model Certification Program

signals.name: Physical Access Devices Not Controlled
signals.description: Physical access devices such as keys, badges, and combinations are not managed throughout their lifecycle. This signal indicates that lost or compromised access devices may provide unauthorized physical access.
signals.applicability: Applicable to all physical access control devices. Includes key management, badge inventory, combination changes, and access device revocation.

metadata.detection_notes: Detected through access device inventory review, key management procedure assessment, and badge lifecycle verification.

sources.title: 32 CFR Part 170 - Cybersecurity Maturity Model Certification Program

signals.name: Physical Security Monitoring Not Implemented
signals.description: Physical security monitoring through cameras, alarms, or guards is not implemented for facilities containing CUI. This signal indicates that physical security incidents may go undetected.
signals.applicability: Applicable to all facilities requiring physical monitoring. Includes CCTV systems, intrusion alarms, security guards, and environmental monitoring systems.

metadata.detection_notes: Detected through security monitoring system review, surveillance coverage assessment, and alarm system verification.

sources.title: 32 CFR Part 170 - Cybersecurity Maturity Model Certification Program

signals.name: Visitor Access Not Controlled
signals.description: Visitors are not authenticated, escorted, or monitored while in facilities containing CUI. This signal indicates that unauthorized access by visitors may go undetected.
signals.applicability: Applicable to all visitor management procedures. Includes visitor sign-in, badge issuance, escort requirements, and visitor monitoring in secure areas.

metadata.detection_notes: Detected through visitor management procedure review, escort policy verification, and visitor log assessment.

sources.title: 32 CFR Part 170 - Cybersecurity Maturity Model Certification Program

signals.name: Risk Assessment Not Conducted
signals.description: The organization has not conducted periodic risk assessments to identify threats, vulnerabilities, and potential impacts to systems and data. This signal indicates that security risks may not be formally identified, documented, or prioritized.
signals.applicability: Applicable to organizational risk management processes including threat identification, vulnerability assessment, impact analysis, and risk prioritization activities.

metadata.detection_notes: Detected through review of risk assessment documentation, assessment schedules, risk registers, and risk management processes.

sources.title: 32 CFR Part 170 - Cybersecurity Maturity Model Certification Program

signals.name: Vulnerability Remediation Not Performed
signals.description: Identified vulnerabilities are not remediated in a timely manner according to risk priorities. This signal indicates that known security weaknesses may persist and remain exploitable.
signals.applicability: Applicable to all vulnerability management processes. Includes patching timelines, remediation tracking, and vulnerability lifecycle management.

metadata.detection_notes: Detected through vulnerability age analysis, remediation SLA verification, and patch compliance assessment.

sources.title: 32 CFR Part 170 - Cybersecurity Maturity Model Certification Program

signals.name: Vulnerability Scanning Not Implemented
signals.description: Systems are not regularly scanned for security vulnerabilities using automated tools. This signal indicates that known vulnerabilities in systems, applications, or configurations may exist without being identified.
signals.applicability: Applicable to all networked systems, applications, and infrastructure components. Includes network vulnerability scanning, web application scanning, container image scanning, and cloud configuration assessment.

metadata.detection_notes: Detected through review of vulnerability scanning schedules, scanner configurations, scan coverage reports, and remediation tracking.
